verifications.claim: Francia (or the Frankish Kingdom) was the largest post-Roman Germanic kingdom in Western Europe.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Francia, also called the Kingdom of the Franks, was the largest post-Roman kingdom in Western Europe.' R2: 'The Kingdom of the Franks... was the largest post-Roman kingdom in Western Europe.'
verifications.reasoning: Both R1 and R2 directly state Francia as the largest post-Roman kingdom in Western Europe; R2 specifies 'Frankish' and Germanic context.

verifications.claim: Francia was established by the Franks in 481 AD.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'In 481, the Roman province of Gaul was established as the Kingdom of Francia'. R2: 'Kingdom of the Franks... c. 481–843 Established c. 481' and 'established by the Franks'.
verifications.reasoning: R1 and R2 explicitly date establishment to 481 AD by the Franks.

verifications.claim: Francia was founded by Clovis I.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Its founder was King Clovis I who united Frankish tribes and expanded the Frankish realm into the Roman Gaul.'
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly identifies Clovis I as the founder of Francia.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'In 481, the Roman province of Gaul was established as the Kingdom of Francia'. R2: 'expanded the Frankish realm into the Roman Gaul.'
verifications.reasoning: Both references confirm expansion/origin from Roman Gaul.

verifications.claim: Francia eventually divided into West Francia (modern France) and East Francia (modern Germany) following the split of Charlemagne's empire.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'After the Treaty of Verdun in 843, it split into West, East, and Middle Francia. East and West Francia would eventually become Germany and France respectively'. R2: 'Treaty of Verdun... West Francia... Kingdom of France... East Francia... Kingdom of Germany'. R3: 'Middle Francia... created in 843 by the Treaty of Verdun... West Francia (which became the Kingdom of France) and East Francia (which became the Kingdom of Germany)'.
verifications.reasoning: References detail the Treaty of Verdun division post-Charlemagne into West Francia (France) and East Francia (Germany), with Middle Francia noted.
